code.originalText: Six-month blood pressure and chronic kidney disease review

text.paragraph: Six-month blood pressure and chronic kidney disease review. [S]

Mr. Washington returns for his six-month review. The back strain in August cleared in about ten days, and he has taken no NSAIDs since. His home readings run in the high 110s to low 120s systolic, with no dizziness on standing. His headaches have not returned, and his concentration is better than in the spring, though he still tires by evening on travel days. He walks 20 to 30 minutes on most days at home. He gets up once a night to urinate and has had no genital symptoms on dapagliflozin. He received the influenza and first zoster vaccines last month. He asked last month to learn more about what would happen if his kidney function fell further. [S]

Severe hypertension with hypertensive kidney disease, at target (I12.9). Standardized office blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, meeting the KDIGO systolic target below 120 without dizziness. [S]

Chronic kidney disease stage G3b A3 (N18.32). eGFR 32, stable after the early dip (36 at diagnosis, 30 on full therapy); urine albumin-creatinine ratio 240 mg/g, down 71 percent from 820; potassium 4.5 and bicarbonate 23. Kidney failure risk 6.5 percent at 2 years and 18.8 percent at 5 years: high. The 5-year risk is above the threshold for nephrology care, and the 2-year risk is below 10 percent. [S]
Continue losartan 100 mg and dapagliflozin 10 mg.
Send today's results and risk scores to nephrology for his next review, with his request to discuss dialysis and conservative care.
